activity.title: Anker and I went through Y Combinator in the summer of 2024. It's one of the best things we've ever done, and I'd recommend it to any early-stage founder. Growing up in Denmark, we had only ever read about Silicon Valley. It felt like a mystical place where people built things we couldn't. YC taught us a lot, but the most important lesson was that we can build something big if we work hard (and smart) enough. That's what gave us the confidence to pivot into AI customer support in the middle of the batch, even though the market was already crowded. Two years (and a lot of late nights) later, Parahelp agents have resolved millions of customer issues for the world’s fastest-growing companies like Cursor and Replit . We'll both be at the YC Internship Expo this Saturday. If you want to help build Parahelp into the leading AI support platform, come talk to us: https://yc.link/r/DcTHZS3h

When your product ships daily, how do you keep an AI support agent up to date? We just released Parahelp automations for support operations tasks like this. Here's how you build an automation that updates your agent whenever relevant parts of your GitHub codebase change.

I’m excited to share that I’m joining Parahelp (YC S24) where I’ll be building their post-sales function - the Customer Acceleration team. Parahelp is the #1 solution for fast moving tech companies that want to automate their customer support & operations workflows with AI. Some of the coolest companies out there like Cursor , Lovable , Replit & Supabase already use Parahelp today! Interested in joining that list of cool companies or simply want to learn more about the product or the team? Shoot me a dm! PS: Always looking for great talent that’s up for a challenge 😜

If a tool has an API, you can connect it to your AI support agent by chatting with Parahelp . Here's how I build a Linear connection so our support agent can handle feature requests the same way we do.

Lots of other AI support solutions are now claiming to be self-improving. By this, they mean once their AI makes a mistake (in production), then it might learn from it. They don't mean proactively in the moment when something changes. This is a minor issue for companies that rarely change such as hotels or airlines (which is what they’re built for), but it makes it completely broken for startups where things constantly change. Given how fast our customers evolve at Parahelp , we’ve built Parahelp to proactively change when your company does. This includes company announcements in Slack, new PRs being merged in GitHub, Notion page updates, Linear tickets, and much much more. Learning from your mistakes is great, but overrated. Proactively learning when your company evolves is the only way to actually provide delightful customer experiences at fast-moving startups.

Today, we're launching Parahelp 3. Intelligence is no longer the bottleneck for AI resolving support tickets - context and tool connections are. Parahelp 3 solves both: - Automations that update your AI support agent whenever your product and policies change - Coding capabilities that let Parahelp build reliable, scoped connections to any tool with an API You build and run your AI support agent on Parahelp to resolve even your most complex tickets end-to-end. Thanks to everyone who has helped us get this far. We're very excited about the next chapter! Read more in the comments.

Expedite has been helping the Parahelp (YC S24) team expand to the US. Parahelp is already trusted by teams like Perplexity, Cursor and Replit, and backed by an $18M Series A led by Alt Capital with participation from Y Combinator and Hanabi Capital. Helping founders like this build in the US is the whole reason we started Expedite. SF is lucky to have you. congrats team 🚀

My biggest concern when I first thought about joining Parahelp was the market. Anker and Mads were so obviously impressive, but customer support seemed like arguably the single worst market to enter. Seemingly half of the latest YC cohorts had been AI customer support solutions, competitors were well-funded, and everyone had recognised it as a great market - clearly the market was lost already. It took me a bit to fully internalise, but none of the other AI customer support solutions actually work for fast-moving tech companies. This might sound ludicrous to anyone who hasn’t tried them, but it is obviously true for anyone who has. Typically this doesn't materialise in direct dislike of the tools, but more “XYZ tool is great, it just doesn’t work for us since we don’t have time to set it up, keep it up to date, and using our tools is too complex.” This is because customer support in tech is a completely different role compared to non-tech, which was immediately evident when I actually went and talked with support leaders. Other solutions fail for two reasons 1. Things constantly change. New launches lead to new bugs, features, and edge cases. If this needs to be manually changed, reviewed, and tested - then your solution will fail immediately. 2. Needs are much more complex. The average support ticket involves looking up customer information in different systems, making a judgment based on the information, and performing actions in different tools. At Parahelp, we have deliberately chosen only to work with fast-moving tech companies. No airlines, hotels, or ecommerce. Instead, we focused entirely on the fastest-moving companies with the most complex tickets. Today, this includes Cursor , Lovable , Perplexity , Replit , Framer , Supabase , Fyxer , HeyGen , Speak , Public , OpusClip , bolt.new , Conductor , Mintlify , and many more. For our customers, we solve up to 92% of all customer support tickets end-to-end. We're able to do this since Parahelp uses your tools to look up customer information (e.g. Datadog logs), perform actions (e.g. issue a refund, change your account settings), and automatically keep itself up to date as your product changes (e.g. updating configurations when you merge a PR in GitHub ). Think your customer interactions are too complex? Drop me a DM.

activity.title: 20 months ago I joined a small startup in Stockholm. Today it's valued at $13.3B. When I told people I was joining Lovable in early 2025, the reaction was mostly "joining what?" We'd just had the launch that changed everything, but to most of the world we were still an unknown Swedish team with a strong conviction: anyone should be able to build software. What stood out to me from the beginning was our users. These were people who'd always had ideas but never a path to bring them to life. Back then, you could build a landing page or a small product. Anything more ambitious was a struggle (if you were there, you know the pain). But every day since, the ceiling of what people can build has risen. Now I watch founders build and scale real businesses on Lovable. I see teams shipping products they once would have hired agencies to build. I see people inside the world's biggest enterprises ship internal tools in days instead of quarters. The gap between "I have an idea" and "I have a business" is collapsing. That valuation comes with a $400M Series C, announced today. In those 18 months: → 60M+ projects created → 900M monthly visits to Lovable-built apps → Builders at nearly two-thirds of the Fortune 500 Joining that crazy team in Stockholm was the best decision I've ever made. Building our product experience team from scratch has been the hardest, most fun work of my life. And the wildest part? All of this is still day 0 🎥 Full story: https://lnkd.in/drqjRZpY We're hiring across the board, come build the thing that lets everyone else build.

We're hiring at Sumary ! Three open roles: GTM Lead, DACH (London based) - German-speaking, owning our entry into Germany end to end. Ex MBB, VC, IB or fintech GTM. Forward Deployed Accountants (Copenhagen, or London based) - smart, outgoing accountants and auditors; a mix of customer success and implementation, working directly with controllers, bookkeepers and CFOs. Fullstack / ML Engineers (Copenhagen based) - build the AI that closes the books. Join a team of full stack devs and ML PhDs. Interested? DM me Pascar Bastian Lucas Frederik

activity.title: I was the youngest employee at Sana when I joined, at Parahelp I’m the oldest. I just turned 26… There are actually more similarities between the two, then differences - other than the fact that both are Scandinavian. Extreme talent. When I joined Sana, I was so impressed by the team and constantly felt like an imposter. Sana managed to hire some of the most amazing people, including Anton Osika - who unfortunately left before I joined. Parahelp managed to do that too: Mads , Anker and the rest of the team are top notch. The main difference is that we are fully AI enabled at Parahelp, allowing us to do far more with less headcount. Everything is automated and efficient - a truly impressive setup. Customer obsession. I’ve rarely seen companies care as much as they do. At Sana we would call our customers partners, since that’s how we truly viewed them. The Impact (Engagement) team would go above and beyond to make a customer win and pulled out some all nighters once in a while - myself included. In hindsight, our lives would have been significantly easier if we would have used Parahelp from the start. It would have saved us countless of hours… That same care is very visible at Parahelp. No matter if you’re a member of the Customer Acceleration team or not, everyone takes initiatives to respond to our customers within seconds. Even our founders - sometime I think they’re just AI bots given how quick they spot things… Incredible products. I remember the first time I touched Sana. It felt like a magical experience, it made me happy and brought me joy. Same thing with Parahelp. I’m so impressed by the intelligence of our agents and how capable it is. Yesterday I built an entire new integration for a customer with the agent. This would normally have taken me a couple of days, with Parahelp I did it in two hours! I feel extremely lucky to have been part of both! My footprint at Sana was left, now it’s time to do the same at Parahelp. 🚀

activity.title: At byFounders , before making any investment, we would always ask ourselves: "would you work for this company?" After leading the investment last year, I decided now was the time to join the most ambitious team I knew, and managed to convince Pascar and the incredible founding team to let me join Sumary 's journey. After spending the past 4.5 years at byFounders leading investments and working with some of the most ambitious founders in the New Nordics, I'm excited to join Sumary as their Chief of Staff, working across gtm, ops and strategy. We're building AI superpowers for accounting professionals and finance teams, and scaling aggressively across Europe. Thanks for the past 4.5 years — Eric , Sara , Martin , Magnus and the rest of the byFounders team. Luckily for me, I get to stay a small part of the byFounders family, as I've now also joined the byFounders angel program. If you're interested in what we're building at Sumary, check out sumary.com or DM me with any questions (we are hiring many roles!).
